Not a bad deck, but it has its limits. This deck is pretty decent but I feel it's a little overhyped. Would I buy the full version? Probably. But would I use it for all of my inquiries? Not exactly. Now, I do think that the Wisdom of the Oracle deck is better than a lot of decks in the AppStore, including the Doreen Virtue ones, however like any oracle or tarot deck, it has its limits. And whether or not it will work for you depends on your own personal connection with the deck. 

Pros:
-There's a large number of cards, and the 7-day trial gives you access to all of them
-The reading formats are all very good. I especially like the five-card spread
-The fact that the cards can be reversed really enhances the message
-There's multiple meanings for the cards, depending on the context of the question (general, relationship, and prosperity for upright, protection for reversed). This leads to more in-depth readings than what other decks on the AppStore provide
-The illustrations are beautiful!

Cons:
-This deck is far better suited for "here and now" questions than predictive ones (but that's how most oracle decks are). My belief is that predictions are based on the energy of the precise moment in which you ask the question, and that you can change the future at any time anyway. Don't waste your time with long-term predictive questions, as the answer will likely change. 
-I've said in other reviews that I hate decks that are overly positive or overly negative. This one is slightly too "doom and gloom" for me. There's significantly more negative to neutral cards in this deck than positive ones, and I've found that most readings I gave were rather dark and heavy (especially the ones for myself- eek!) Honestly, I don't like that kind of energy from a deck. To me it's just as bad as light and fluffy feel-good readings.

All in all, this deck would get 3.5 stars from me. It's a decent deck to have in your collection but I wouldn't consider it my end-all, be-all, as the accuracy isn't 100%.
